messages:
Support Bot: Escalation from Acme Corp — they saw intermittent 500s and sustained latency spike (~600ms to 2s) starting 2026-02-03T14:12Z during a pen test. Pen team reported repeated KMS errors and a large jump in token calls. They attached a couple of logs.
Alex P: Thanks — can you paste the specific error lines and a minimal repro? tagging @Samir and @Maya R for infra/security context.
Jamie L: Customer provided this snippet: `ERROR inference.service: failed to fetch data-key: ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded` and several `403: KMS AccessDenied` mixed in. Billing showed ~3.2x token ops during the window.
Samir: Quick thought: looks like the client is doing per-request data-key generation instead of caching the data key. If the pen test created many parallel sessions that can spike KMS ops. Example anti-pattern we see:
```
for r in requests:
  key = kms.describe_key('alias/app')
  dk = kms.generate_data_key(KeyId=key)
  call_inference(dk)
```
Maya R: That pattern can surface during stress tests. From a security standpoint we need to validate whether the pen test found an actual auth bypass or just resource exhaustion. Pen report claims "KMS HSM negotiation failures allow request retries to bypass rate limits" — need concrete repro.
Leah C: Pulled KMS metrics: ThrottledRequests spike at 14:11:32 -> 14:14:05, ConcurrentConnections also peaked. CloudTrail snippet (redacted): "\"eventName\": \"GenerateDataKey\", \"errorCode\": \"ThrottlingException\", \"sourceIPAddress\": \"203.0.113.45\"" repeated ~2600 times in 3m.
Jamie L: Customer billing screenshot shows token ops from service account `svc-acme-prod` jumped. They say it started right after their pen test kickoff. They want us to confirm whether keys were exposed. They also want mitigation ASAP.
Alex P: Operational mitigation first: can we enable local data-key caching on the SDK and increase KMS client-side concurrency limits? Also add a short TTL cache for DescribeKey results so we avoid alias lookups.
Samir: Agree. I can ship a small client-side patch (2-line change) to cache data-keys for 5s and add exponential backoff on generate_data_key. Will roll it to a canary within the hour.
Maya R: For the security posture: pen team labeled as HIGH because they claim "alias enumeration + throttling could be chained to a timing attack against HSM vendor firmware". I don't see a credible exploit without privileged access to the HSM admin plane. Proposal: classify as MEDIUM pending vendor HSM log review and retest.
Jamie L: Customer is pushing for higher severity. They want evidence we collected: CloudTrail, KMS metric graphs, pod logs, and HSM vendor session logs. I can collate CloudTrail + pod logs into the secure folder.
Leah C: I can request the HSM vendor logs; need approval because those are off our regular ticket flow. @Maya R can you confirm we should escalate to vendor support? We might need a signed NDA for raw HSM session traces.
Maya R: Yes escalate. Send vendor request template IAW our process. We'll request session-level traces for the 14:10-14:20 window only.
Alex P: Action list: 1) Samir — deploy client-side caching + backoff canary (ETA: 1h) 2) Jamie — package CloudTrail, pod logs, billing snapshot to secure share (ETA: 2h) 3) Leah — request HSM vendor logs + confirm access path (ETA: 4h) 4) Maya/Security — re-evaluate severity after vendor logs and retest (ETA: after logs). I set a retest target 48h after mitigations.
Samir: Deployed canary to 10% -> telemetry shows ThrottledRequests dropped 85% in canary. :white_check_mark:
Jamie L: Uploaded artifacts to secure share (link redacted) and notified Acme. Included sample CloudTrail, billing screenshot, pod stdout with stack traces.
Maya R: Reviewed artifacts, vendor has accepted the request for session logs. Preliminary read: no sign of key material exfiltration. Escalation severity updated to MEDIUM. We'll proceed with vendor logs and then schedule pen-test retest.
Support Bot: Noted. Customer notified of MEDIUM classification and planned retest in 48h. Next steps: collect vendor logs and confirm retest window. :thumbsup:
Alex P: Thanks everyone. Please append any further findings to this thread. We'll close once retest passes and we have vendor confirmation.
